category_title: Students who engage in disruptive behavior to avoid difficult academic tasks
minimal_context: David is presented with a reading assignment during his English Language Arts class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: David, it is time for ELA. Please read this passage and complete the assignment at your desk.

STUDENT: (Stares at the paper) I'm not reading this. It's too long.

TUTOR: You need to do your work. Just get started.

STUDENT: (Pushes the assignment off the desk) No! I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: David, pick up your paper right now or I will have to send you to the office.

STUDENT: I don't give a s***! Send me to the office, I'm not doing this f***ing reading!

options.A: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level reading questions based on the student's level, providing a higher percentage of lower-level questions.
options.B: Allow the student to choose their own creative reading projects based on their personal strengths and interests during the ELA period.
options.C: Establish a classroom reading community founded on mutual respect for student choice and individual perspectives during daily ELA assignments.
options.D: Implement a contingency contract outlining behavioral expectations, where the student earns points for completing assignments and finishing lessons without using inappropriate language.
